X.note: The three cubes are nearly the same size, so 7%, 6% and 13% can't be compared by height. The 13% card is semi-transparent and sits on the cube, so its text is low-contrast and muddy. The left label covers the orange cube. The 'ACTUAL' tag repeats four times and means nothing to a viewer. The dark empty grid floor wastes space. The cards read as flat UI boxes.

Y.note: Real terrain with a river, and a readable 'Delaware River valley' place tag. One coin labeled 'world price' next to four coins labeled '≈4× ESTIMATE' shows the ratio at a glance. The coins have white outlines and a decent material, though the terrain looks a bit plain and flat. The labels are clean and high-contrast, and the layout is uncluttered. Minor issues: the coins are small, a coin is a slightly odd metaphor for a tanker, and the bottom caption area is a dead dark band.

why: Y shows the 1-vs-4 ratio at a glance in a clear place context with clean, legible labels, while X has overlapping, partly transparent labels and cubes that don't visually match their numbers.
top_fix_for_weaker: Scale the cube heights to 6/7/13 so the 13% bar is about twice as tall as the others. Put the labels above or beside each bar with solid opaque cards and no overlap. Drop the repeated 'ACTUAL' tags. Add a ground reference or scene context instead of the empty dark grid.
